feature: A pinch on the hour-long timeline lays each lane's new picture between frames
summary: When a pinch moves the timeline on to a new scale, each lane now shows its last picture for that one frame and draws the new one in the gap before the next frame. Near the whole-hour view about a fifth fewer frames are late. Nothing about how the timeline looks at rest changed.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The button on step 1 opens your own copy of the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev; File > Open reaches it too (Cmd-Shift-G, ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev). Measured with a timeline-only speed walk on the probe, one build with a throwaway switch, three runs each way.

try.do: Open the 60 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below.
Press Backslash to see the whole hour.
Pinch the timeline in quickly, a few times.
Pinch in again quickly, then stop.
Scroll sideways along the timeline with two fingers.

evaluate: Does a quick pinch near the whole-hour view feel smoother than yesterday?
When the pinch stops, do clip names, cuts and the Music lane's fade diamonds settle at once, with no flash?
Does sideways scrolling feel as it did before?
rough: Numbers, 60 minute edit, one build, throwaway switch, three runs each way (load about 3.5): near Fit late frames 122/129/124 to 113/94/89 of 648, mean frame 9.60/9.59/9.70 to 9.27/9.26/9.01 ms, p95 16.7 to 15.9/15.9/14.8; zoom out late 21/15/13 to 14/12/10 of 240; zoom in unchanged (46/40/47 to 42/46/49); scroll unchanged (9/12/14 to 10/13/10 of 360).

Tried and not kept: laying the late picture from a main queue block (it ran before the frame went out, so the frame was no shorter and scroll got worse, 9 to 13 late to 82 to 89); laying a scroll's step late too (16 to 27 late against 9 to 13); drawing pictures into a Core Graphics context of our own (four times slower than the renderer in use).
Every lane's picture is drawn again on the frame the timeline stops moving, a one-off cost of about 3 ms at the stop, so nothing a late picture missed stays on screen.

Bars of the task not reached: near Fit still about 15 per cent of frames late (the frames that let go of a held painting, about 13 ms each, now mostly SwiftUI rebuilding the lanes), zoom in about 45 of 240, edits (owned by a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed). The task stays open.
No mock covers the timeline's speed; nothing about the timeline's resting look changed.
